**Why the swap.** `domain:cloud` is not in the SKILL.md lane table, so it names no seat. Under the seat post's standing instruction ⑤ (self-invented `domain:*` labels are stripped at triage and re-routed under the anchoring rule — `domain:*` has exactly one producer), it comes off. ⇒ replaced with **`repo:cloud`**, which is a real routing target with a real seat behind it.

⚠️ This mattered rather than being cosmetic: a `pm:queue` card whose only routing label names no lane is **invisible to every candidate query in the fleet**. It reads as queued and is reachable by nobody. This card has been in that state since it was filed at 06:18Z.

⛔ `domain:cloud` had not been seen in circulation before today; I have added it to the seat post's list of known self-invented label objects (⑤) so the next sweep recognises the shape. The label **object** still exists in the repo and autocomplete will keep offering it — deleting it is a separate step, and until then every sweep treats it as a half-annotation.

**Named reader (a `repo:*` label without one is a queue nobody scans): the `repo:cloud` execution seat, seat post #6026.**

**Routing test**: strip objectstack out of the card and it still stands — the census runs entirely inside `objectstack-ai/cloud`, and the card says plainly that no objectstack seat can reach that repo. ⇒ seam card: stays here, carries `repo:cloud`, names its reader. Same shape as #14187, routed identically in this round.

**Grade p2, and the timing constraint is the reason it is not p3**: the card asks for the census *before* `cloud`'s next `.objectstack-sha` bump. ⇒ this has a **moving deadline set by someone else's cadence**, and it becomes worthless if the bump lands first. ⚠️ The `repo:cloud` seat should sequence it against its own pin schedule — its seat post currently reports pin `afbf2711` with a bridge, so the window is open but ⛔ not indefinitely.

**Dedup**: this is the ADR-0111 `CODE:` prefix-consumer census for the `cloud` population specifically. ⛔ No duplicate — the in-repo half is a different population and is not what this card asks for.

## READING — ADR-0111 `CODE:` prefix-consumer census in `objectstack-ai/cloud`

`repo:cloud` execution seat (seat post #6026), session `session_017Wu48ZSjk7HJjyJmGNBtUk`, PM loop R35 reading batch C. ⛔ Read-only: no branch, no worktree edit, no install, no build, no PR. `git status --porcelain` on the reading tree is empty.

**Tree measured.** `objectstack-ai/cloud` `origin/main` at **`9b6abe0f2fd58e39f1f5ca329940f5cf5d75f50d`** (`9b6abe0`, "feat(cloud): publish the control plane upgrade entry as an absolute upgradeUrl, from one console-URL producer (#1870)"), read in a detached read-only worktree. Its framework pin `.objectstack-sha` = **`655b106ce2804d2cdb9ed4386df795152535d372`**.

⚠️ **Timing, corrected against the card's premise.** The card asks for the census *before* cloud's next `.objectstack-sha` bump past PR #14120. That window has **already closed**: the pin above was bumped by cloud PR #1868 on 2026-09-02, and REST compare shows PR #14120's merge commit `bb4ea805` **is an ancestor** of `655b106c` (pin 228 ahead, 0 behind). ⇒ The 4xx `CODE:` strip is **live in cloud today**, and this reading is the **exposure check**, not the pre-bump check.

### VERDICT: ZERO branching consumers. The premise holds in `cloud`.

⛔ Not a bare zero — every zero below sits beside a control that fired on this same tree.

### Scope

Whole repo, all tracked files, `node_modules/`, `dist/` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` excluded. **Control G**: `git ls-files | grep -vE "node_modules|/dist/" | wc -l` = **1624** tracked files; `git ls-files -- '*.ts' '*.tsx' | grep -v node_modules | wc -l` = **905** TS/TSX files. Tests are **included and attributed**, per the card.

Six declared ADR-0111 codes throughout: `VALIDATION_FAILED`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `NOT_FOUND`, `CONFLICT`, `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED`, `FORBIDDEN`.

### The ready-made command (comment 5475900981's runnable form), verbatim result

```
$ git grep -nE "startsWith\(\s*['\"\`](VALIDATION_FAILED|PERMISSION_DENIED|NOT_FOUND|CONFLICT|SHARING_NOT_ENABLED|FORBIDDEN)" -- '*.ts' '*.tsx'
P1 exit=1
```

**0 hits.** ⛔ On its own that is an artefact risk, which is why the eleven-pattern widening and five controls below exist.

### Every pattern run, and what each returned

| # | pattern | hits | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | `startsWith(` on a quoted declared code (the ready-made command) | **0** | — |
| P2 | `includes(` / `indexOf(` on a `CODE:` literal | **0** | — |
| P3 | ANY quoted literal placing a declared code immediately before `:` (ts, tsx, js, mjs, md, mdx) | **1** | producer, not consumer |
| P4 | `replace(` / `replaceAll(` carrying a `CODE:` literal or a SCREAMING_SNAKE-colon regex — the objectui scrubber shape | **0** | — |
| P5 | any regex literal of the shape "uppercase run then colon" | **4** | none touch an error string |
| P6 | `.split(':')` / `.split('://')` | **5** | all host:port or URL scheme |
| P7 | reads of an `.error` field off a parsed response body | **375** | overwhelmingly `.code`; classified below |
| P8 | `startsWith` / `includes` / `indexOf` on an error-, message-, reason- or body-shaped receiver | **20** | all unanchored, none prefix-anchored |
| P9 | regex `test` / `match` / `exec` against an error- or message-shaped receiver | **19** | all unanchored substring shapes |
| P10 | regex **literals** containing one of the six codes | **8** | 3 in-process test assertions, 5 prose/comment |
| P11 | a `CODE:` literal in json / yaml / yml / sql | **0** | — |

### Positive controls, quoted, all on `9b6abe0`

- **Control A** (for P1): `git grep -nE "\.startsWith\(" -- '*.ts' '*.tsx' | wc -l` → **218**
- **Control B** (for P2): `git grep -nE "\.includes\(" -- '*.ts' '*.tsx' | wc -l` → **286**
- **Control C** (for P4): `git grep -nE "\.(replace|replaceAll)\(" -- '*.ts' '*.tsx' | wc -l` → **165**
- **Control D** (for P6): `git grep -nE "\.split\(" -- '*.ts' '*.tsx' | wc -l` → **241**
- ⭐ **Control E, the one that makes the zero a reading** (for P1/P2/P3/P11): the six declared codes are **not absent from this tree** — `git grep -ncE "VALIDATION_FAILED|PERMISSION_DENIED|NOT_FOUND|CONFLICT|SHARING_NOT_ENABLED|FORBIDDEN"` over ts, tsx, md, mdx, json sums to **166 occurrences across 54 files**. So the codes are everywhere in `cloud`; what is absent is any use of one **as a prefix token read off a wire string**. A pattern that could not have matched would have returned 0 here too.

Controls A–D each returned a healthy non-zero on the same invocation shape as the pattern they control, so P1, P2, P4 and P11's zeros are readings.

### Attribution of every hit that touches an error string

**P3 — the single `CODE:` string literal in the repo. PRODUCER, runtime.**
`packages/service-cloud/src/control-plane-org-scope-plugin.ts:657`
```ts
const err: any = new Error(
    `PERMISSION_DENIED: ${operation} on '${object}' targets a record outside your organizations`,
);
err.code = 'PERMISSION_DENIED';
err.status = 403;
```
cloud **writes** the prefix here; it does not read one. Its own docblock says the REST layer "already translates by matching on `code`". This is the ADR-0112 producer shape, unaffected by a consumer-side strip.

**P7 — 375 `.error` reads, classified.** The dominant shape is structured and prefix-blind: `body?.error?.code`, and the dialect-tolerant `body?.error?.code ?? body?.code` (e.g. `apps/cloud/test/unscoped-control-plane-tenant-wall.test.ts:983,997,1008,1024,1450,1459,1682,1698`; `apps/ee-group-showcase/test/depth-sharing-authority.dogfood.test.ts:116`; `packages/security-enterprise/src/license/online-client.ts:408`). ⇒ These read the **`code` field**, never the human `error` string, so the strip is invisible to them. That `??` is object-vs-object dialect tolerance, **not** `error.code`-vs-`error`-string branching.

⭐ **The one genuine WIRE `error`-STRING consumer in the whole repo — and it is tolerant, not branching. TEST, runtime wire.**
`apps/objectos/test/single-environment-crm-bundle.test.ts:86` and `:110`
```ts
const { status, body } = await call('/api/v1/data/account', { method: 'POST', body: { name: 'BareInvalid', website: 'bogus' } });
assert(status === 400, ...);
assert(
    typeof body?.error === 'string' && /website must start with/i.test(body.error),
    `expected hook error, got ${JSON.stringify(body)}`,
);
```
This really does hit a **4xx `/api/v1/data/…` exit** through `app.fetch` and really does read `body.error` as a **string** — the exact door PR #14120 changed. But the regex is **unanchored** and matches domain wording (`website must start with`) that the strip does not touch; it never required the leading `VALIDATION_FAILED: ` token and never asked where in the string its match sat. ⇒ **Affirmative evidence for the premise**, the same class as the three objectui prefix-`replace` scrubbers the at-tier reviewer found: a tolerant reader that is a no-op after the change.

**P8/P9 — the 39 error-string matchers, all unanchored, none prefix-dependent.** Named because "unanchored" is a claim someone should be able to falsify:
- `packages/service-ai-studio/src/tools/flow-tools.ts:54` `const FLOW_NOT_FOUND_SHAPE = /not\s*found|unknown\s*flow|no\s*such\s*flow/i;` — matched against `String(r.error ?? '')` at `:74`, where `r` is the **in-process** `ctx.automation.execute()` result, not a wire body.
- `packages/service-ai/src/tools/data-tools.ts:1014` `const NOT_FOUND_SHAPE = /not\s*found|unknown\s*object|could\s*not\s*resolve|无法解析/i;` — `\s*` does not match the underscore in `NOT_FOUND`, so the prefix token never contributed a match here either way.
- `packages/service-ai-studio/src/tools/verify-tools.ts:446` — reached **only** when `err.code` is absent: `isDefinitiveMissError` tests `code` first and returns `false` for a named non-miss code before the message fallback. Code-first, message-as-fallback — the safe shape.
- `packages/service-tenant/src/environment-provisioning.ts:68-70` `IDEMPOTENT_RETRY_SIGNATURE` — matches **Turso Platform API** messages, not objectstack wire.
- `packages/service-cloud/src/routes/cloud.ts:422-425`, `packages/service-ai/src/routes/ai-routes.ts:728,780`, `packages/service-ai/src/routes/pending-action-routes.ts:159,160,188,189`, `packages/service-cloud/src/routes/environment-lifecycle.ts:1048,1713`, `packages/service-cloud/src/storage-service-blob-store.ts:63,79`, `apps/cloud/server/index.ts:177`, `apps/objectos/server/index.ts:302` — all **in-process** `err.message` inspection inside cloud's own catch blocks, on errors cloud's own process threw or its own driver raised. In-process messages are not what `resolveErrorResponse`'s 4xx arm rewrites.

**P10 — the three assertions that DO name a code inside a regex. TEST, in-process, not wire.**
`apps/ee-group-showcase/test/cross-org-approval.dogfood.test.ts:264,270,276`
```ts
).rejects.toThrow(/VALIDATION_FAILED.*not in the same group/);
```
⚠️ This is the closest thing in `cloud` to a prefix-dependent reader, so it is named rather than folded into a total. It is **not** a wire consumer: `openRequest` at `:87` calls `approvals.openNodeRequest(...)` — a direct in-process service call on the booted stack — so it asserts on a thrown `Error.message`, which the wire 4xx serialization never touches. The remaining P10 hits (`apps/cloud/test/control-plane-default-profile.test.ts:332,361`, `packages/service-ai-studio/src/skills/metadata-authoring-skill.ts:338,341`, `scripts/check-docs-error-codes.mjs:106`) are **prose** — comments and skill copy where `FORBIDDEN` is an English word or a docs-gate synonym list.

**P5/P6 — non-error, for completeness.** `apps/cloud/cloudflare/config-guard.ts:120` and `apps/objectos/cloudflare/config-guard.ts:120` are URL-scheme regexes; `packages/objectos-runtime/src/build-trace.ts:59` and `packages/service-cloud/src/fault-log.ts:68` are word-segment regexes; the five `split` hits (`apps/objectos/server/index.ts:158`, `packages/objectos-runtime/src/{ai-token-guardrail-plugin.ts:107,ai-usage-endpoint-plugin.ts:230,kernel-resolver.ts:180}`, `apps/cloud/scripts/drill-r2-readpath.ts:46`) all strip a port or a URL scheme off a **host**, never off an error string.

### What this closes

| repo | result | control |
|---|---|---|
| objectstack | zero branching consumers outside `rest` | 7 |
| objectui | zero | 491 `startsWith(` lines read |
| hotcrm | zero | 79 |
| **`objectstack-ai/cloud`** | ⭐ **zero branching consumers** — 1 producer, 1 tolerant wire reader, 3 in-process test assertions | **218 / 286 / 165 / 241, plus 166 code occurrences across 54 files** |

⇒ The census the 2026-08-31 ruling on #13095 gated on is now **complete across all four repos**, and every one of them is zero. ⛔ No fork is raised on #13095: the gate was `non-zero ⇒ stop and report a fork`, and this reading is zero. No pointer comment is posted there for a zero result.

⚠️ Honest limit of this reading: it measures `cloud` at `9b6abe0` only. It says nothing about consumers outside these four repos, and nothing about a consumer that reads the `error` string at runtime through a name this static census cannot see (a dynamically built pattern, a value arriving from configuration). Neither shape appears here — but "does not appear in a static census" is what was measured, and it is not the same sentence as "cannot exist".
